evals.prompt: Build a messaging framework for Ledgerline, a treasury tool for crypto-native companies. Positioning: 'The treasury OS for companies that hold stablecoins, with real-time multi-chain balances and audit-ready reports.' Personas: CFO, Head of Finance Ops, external auditor.
evals.expected_output: Should build the capability table first with gaps marked and assumptions under it, then write the hero line for the loosely familiar visitor: walk the decision tree with evidence, choose against or for, write 3 to 5 hero lines with subheads, and recommend one with its source. Then persona translations and three boilerplate lengths.
assertions: Includes a capability table with the columns Capability, What it does for the buyer, Proof, and Buyer voice, with missing proof or quotes marked as gaps inside the table
Every capability named in the positioning statement appears as a row in the capability table (real-time multi-chain balances and audit-ready reports)
Places an Assumptions block directly under the capability table
Puts the capability table before the hero line
Walks the decision tree (category maturity, then the branch questions) and states each answer with its evidence in one line
Names the anchor the decision tree leads to (persona, category, feature, capability, problem, or benefit)
Chooses a frame, against a named alternative or for a job, and says why
Writes 3 to 5 hero lines with subheads that carry capabilities, a number, or the mechanism
Recommends one hero line and cites the research finding behind it, or says the pick is an assumption
Gives a distinct lead capability or first line per persona
Provides boilerplate at three lengths

evals.prompt: Our messaging pillars are: Easy to use, Secure, Scalable, Great support. Fix them. We're a B2B data pipeline tool competing with Fivetran.
evals.expected_output: Identifies missing upstream positioning/differentiation, routes to positioning-strategy or context establishment, and avoids inventing reusable strategy or capabilities. Independent diagnostic work continues.
assertions: Identifies missing upstream strategy or capability evidence
Routes positioning/differentiation to positioning-strategy
Does not invent a reusable position or differentiating capabilities to complete the framework
Continues independent diagnostic work with evidence and approval dependencies separate

evals.expected_output: Should include the launch block (target, market, segment, category, unique value, proof) and language to use and avoid.
assertions: Includes a launch block covering target, category, unique value, and proof
Includes words to use and words to avoid
Avoids clichés such as unlock, seamless, or game-changer
Does not invent resolution-rate statistics as fact
Names capabilities as concrete, verb-led abilities, not abstract nouns such as visibility, insights, intelligence, protection, or platform

evals.prompt: Build our messaging framework. From our context doc. Positioning: 'Ledgerly is a close tool that auto-matches bank lines to invoices for finance teams at 50 to 300 person SaaS companies.' Contextual alternative: Excel macros and manual tick-and-tie. Capability table: auto-matching (proof: beta cut matching time 60%, Sourced); exception queue (Gap). Persona message map: Controller (champion), close speed, 'Close in days, not weeks, because matching runs itself.' (Assumed). No CFO row. Also, I think our SOC 2 report is a differentiator, add that.
evals.expected_output: Should open with Inputs and assumptions, build capability rows only from the positioning table (auto-matching, exception queue), and put SOC 2 under 'Proposed for positioning' without using it in the messaging. Persona lines start from the Controller map row, adapting emphasis only; any CFO line is labeled Assumed with a recommendation to run icp-and-buyer-personas. Includes one cost-of-doing-nothing line from the Excel alternative and ends with Evidence gaps.
assertions: Opens with an Inputs and assumptions section
Capability rows come only from the positioning's capability table: auto-matching and exception queue
Lists SOC 2 under 'Proposed for positioning' and does not use it in the hero line, capability table, persona lines, or boilerplate
The Controller persona line starts from the message map and keeps its facts, changing emphasis only
Routes missing CFO persona understanding to icp-and-buyer-personas instead of inventing reusable persona priorities
Includes one line on the cost of doing nothing tied to Excel macros or manual tick-and-tie
Ends with an Evidence gaps section in the ranked format

evals.prompt: HND-100 from product-marketing-context, GAP-100: determine which messaging work can proceed given this evidence, then return a dependency-aware proposal. No upstream positioning proposal or approved positioning exists. Completion: identify the missing strategic input without inventing it; approved persona is available.
evals.expected_output: Preserves domain ownership and returns scoped findings/proposals or dependencies without upgrading evidence or approval.
assertions: Routes missing positioning to positioning-strategy rather than inferring reusable positioning
Uses the approved persona without creating a new one; permits independent supported work
Returns findings/proposals with source references, scope, method or derivation and limitations
Keeps evidence labels and human approval separate; does not write canon
Returns to product-marketing-context for the originating handoff rather than automatically overwriting bootstrap context

evals.prompt: Using the Aiven packet, build a bounded messaging proposal from this upstream positioning proposal: company role is managed open-source data operations for production AI; initial solution is fresh retrieval context for existing enterprise assistant and agent teams. Candidate value is operating continuity across their existing data services and deployment choices, with comparative outcome proof still missing. Compare messaging hierarchies, select one, translate for the buying committee and provide an existing-customer sales-play handoff. Do not invent a new differentiator or save canon.
evals.expected_output: Preserves company/solution levels and uncertainty, makes persona differences matter, turns a scoped advantage into customer value, and separates internal evidence trace from applied copy.
assertions: Keeps company narrative distinct from beachhead-specific value and does not turn one assistant use case into the whole company position
Compares at least two messaging hierarchies and explains the selected emphasis with buyer criteria and proof limitations
Each leading pillar connects buyer outcome, named alternative or status quo, supporting capability and proof requirement without false exclusivity
Includes distinct application/business owner and infrastructure owner messages, reflecting outcome versus operating priorities and unresolved budget
Provides natural applied copy whose claims stay within supplied capability and maturity boundaries; keeps evidence labels in internal trace rather than repeating them in every sentence
Connects selected messaging to discovery, stakeholder alignment, technical evaluation and conversion evidence in a concise sales-play handoff
Does not claim guaranteed freshness, end-to-end access control, comparative savings, shipped integrated diagnosis or validated customer demand
Does not use internal strategy phrases such as installed-base leverage or validation gate as customer-facing benefits
Tests headline and subhead together against named alternatives and exposes the selected buying reason in primary value, while permitting shared supporting pillars

evals.prompt: Build SecureBuild messaging from this upstream proposal: governed exception continuity across CI systems for multi-CI container teams. Use the supplied profiles and product evidence, compare two hierarchies, then provide persona messages and two applied sales lines. This is a provisional proposal, not approved canon.
evals.expected_output: Uses the product capability to express credible buyer value, reflects security and release priorities, respects competing strengths and proof limits.
assertions: Expresses customer value from cross-CI signed exception continuity instead of generic secure/scalable messaging
Separates security accountability from platform implementation and application release continuity in persona messaging
Treats MegaSec broader coverage as a real advantage and avoids unsupported category leadership or universal superiority
Uses controlled pilot evidence within its stated scope and does not invent ROI, breach reduction or paid preference
Explains why the chosen hierarchy beats a credible alternative and connects pillars to capability, buyer criterion and proof
Produces natural applied sales copy consistent with the position without repeating provisional evidence labels in every sentence

evals.prompt: Write only two short renewal-call opening lines for existing SecureBuild platform engineering champions. The accepted message is governed exception continuity across CI systems; shipped capability and controlled pilot proof are in the packet. Keep the scope narrow. Do not propose new positioning, segments or a market study.
evals.expected_output: Produces concise channel-appropriate lines from the named position and persona without reopening market discovery or forcing a company messaging architecture.
assertions: Provides two concise renewal-call opening lines suited to platform engineering and the supplied capability
Does not reopen market discovery, segment selection, positioning territories or a company-level architecture
Does not invent time savings, security outcomes, customer quotes or procurement authority
Keeps supporting uncertainty outside the applied lines unless needed to avoid a misleading claim

evals.prompt: Using only QueueBridge and its upstream positioning proposal, create a bounded messaging framework for the application owner and engineer. Compare two primary message pairs, select one, show the evidence-to-message chain and two sales lines. No new positioning or market discovery.
evals.expected_output: Business translation from the selected comparative preference, not generic events, reliability or feature copy.
assertions: Primary message pair expresses settlement-exception resolution with traceable records across retained processor integrations, not only reliable event processing
Application-owner message addresses correct merchant status or resolving settlement exceptions; engineer message addresses matching, retries and integration trade-offs
Uses competitor substitution to explain why the overall pair is situationally meaningful while allowing shared supporting benefits
Preserves fixture proof only for linked records; does not invent faster resolution, satisfaction, ROI or customer quotes
Shows research insight, buyer tension, selected value, message and proof for the primary pair, with natural applied copy and appropriate next action
